In these circumstances auditors will seek to determine, by agreement with the provider, the potential number of errors, and if appropriate, ask the provider to make a payment on account of the final penalty, while the correct figure is calculated.

The provider must inform each registered contact whose CTF is voided of details of the interest, dividends and capital gains and losses arising on the investments.

These will be taxable on the child in the normal way.

Applications

The auditor will select a sample of CTFs opened by voucher with the provider and view documentation relating to each account selected to verify if the account meets all CTF requirements. For the CTFs selected for examination auditors will check:

that a valid voucher is held (if appropriate)

where the application is in writing that the application is fully completed and contains a signature

where the application is not in writing that a written declaration has been made on behalf of the applicant

that the CTF was not opened prior to receipt of the voucher and completion of the application form

that the application contains the required declaration and authority , and

that the terms and conditions applying to the CTF contain the required statements (read the section on ‘CTF terms and conditions’).

Subscriptions to CTFs

The auditor will examine the provider’s system for preventing oversubscription to the CTF, and will select a sample of CTFs held by the provider. For the CTFs selected for examination auditors will check:

that the subscription limits have not been breached (read the ‘When can subscriptions to a CTF be accepted’ section)

that withdrawals from the CTF have only taken place in allowed circumstances (read the ‘When investments can be withdrawn from a CTF’ section)

Stakeholder CTFs

Where the provider offers stakeholder CTFs auditors will examine the conditions applying to the stakeholder to make sure that they comply with conditions set out in the ‘Stakeholder conditions’ section.

Non-stakeholder CTFs

Auditors will review the investment policy of the CTF provider and look for further documentary evidence that only qualifying investments have been made within the CTF. They will check that the ongoing responsibility for managing the investment strategy within CTF continues and that the investment qualification for CTF is continually monitored.

Auditors will ask for a stock listing (or equivalent) to review the types of investment held in the CTF, and where the auditor is unsure of the qualification of some investments for CTF may ask the provider for evidence that the particular investment qualifies for CTF.

Transferred CTFs

Auditors will check the procedures in place to facilitate the transfer of CTFs out to a new provider and for internal transfers by examining the paperwork for transferred accounts, which will include the request by the registered contact to transfer the CTF. They will check that the transfer was carried out within the time allowed (read the ‘Internal transfer’ and ‘External transfer’ sections).

Interim and annual claims

Auditors will look in detail at the most recent claims submitted, both CTF10 and CTF14, to verify the claims being made are accurate and reflect the amount of tax deducted from investments.

They will need to see any original vouchers relating to claims; verify only the amount stated as tax has been claimed for; and to make sure that claims are made only for investments relating to CTF accounts. There will be a walk through of the system to look at fail-safes of claims procedures and make sure claims relate only to UK income tax deducted.

The CTF14 annual claim form will be examined to verify that it accurately reflects the details of the interim claims for the period and that any balancing charge or claim is accurate and verifiable.

Annual information returns

Auditors will select a sample of CTFs, to verify the information returned on the annual information return is accurate and reflects the information held by the manager.

Auditors will also check that all CTF accounts under management of the provider at 5 April each year appear on the annual return. The auditor will select a sample of accounts from the provider’s database and compare the details with the submitted return to make sure they have been reported correctly.

Annual statements

Auditors will view a sample of the annual statements issued (read the section on CTF statements’), to verify that the details sent to each child are accurate and reflected in the records of the provider. They will also view the statement contents to verify that the detail contained are as required by CTF regulations and make sure the statement has been issued to the appropriate person at the correct time (read the ‘To whom issued’ and ‘Statement contents’ sections).

Qualifying investments

The auditor will check a sample from a listing of all CTF investments (other than cash on deposit) held by the provider, to verify that only qualifying investments are held within the CTF (read the section on ‘Qualifying investments in the CTF’). They will view a stock listing (or equivalent) to review the types of investment held and review systems controlling the investments made within the CTF.

Withdrawals

The auditor will review all accounts where investments have been withdrawn from the CTF, to make sure that withdrawals are allowed only in the circumstances in section ‘When investments can be withdrawn from a CTF’, to verify the procedures and processes for allowing withdrawals are adequately controlled to prevent unauthorised withdrawals.
